definitions.explanation: The leaves of the bamboo grass plant (笹). Used in traditional Japanese culture for decorations, food wrapping, and in the Tanabata festival.

examples.japanese: ⟦{七夕|たなばた}→七夕：05633_tanabata⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{笹|ささ}の{葉|は}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{願|ねが}い{事|ごと}→願い事：14621_negaigoto⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飾|かざ}った→飾る：01185_kazaru⟧。
examples.english: We hung our wishes on bamboo grass leaves for Tanabata.

examples.japanese: {笹|ささ}の{葉|は}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{包|つつ}んだ→包む：01226_tsutsumu⟧⟦お{餅|もち}→お餅：23451_omochi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦もらった→もらう：00520_morau⟧。
examples.english: I received rice cakes wrapped in bamboo grass leaves.

examples.japanese: ⟦{風|かぜ}→風：00641_kaze⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{揺|ゆ}れる→揺れる：01161_yureru⟧{笹|ささ}の{葉|は}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦さらさら→さらさら：05255_sarasara⟧⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦{音|おと}→音：00743_oto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{心地|ここち}よい→心地よい：12515_kokochiyoi⟧。
examples.english: The rustling sound of bamboo grass leaves swaying in the wind is pleasant.

notes: Closely associated with the ⟦{七夕|たなばた}→七夕：05633_tanabata⟧ (Tanabata, Star Festival) on July 7th, when people write wishes on strips of paper (⟦{短冊|たんざく}→短冊：13674_tanzaku⟧) and hang them on {笹|ささ}の{葉|は}. The famous Tanabata song begins with 「{笹|ささ}の{葉|は}⟦さらさら→さらさら：05255_sarasara⟧」 (bamboo leaves rustling). {笹|ささ}の{葉|は} are also used to wrap food items like ⟦{笹団子|ささだんご}→笹団子：28857_sasadango⟧ (bamboo-leaf-wrapped rice dumplings) and as decorative garnishes in Japanese cuisine.
